  "vulnerability_pattern": "Custom sysctl handler calls proc_dointvec but uses output variable without checking return code, violating invariant that parsed value is only valid on success.",
  "patch": "commit 24599e61b7552673dd85971cf5a35369cd8c119e
Author: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Date:   Wed Jun 18 23:46:31 2014 +0200

    net: sctp: check proc_dointvec result in proc_sctp_do_auth
    
    When writing to the sysctl field net.sctp.auth_enable, it can well
    be that the user buffer we handed over to proc_dointvec() via
    proc_sctp_do_auth() handler contains something other than integers.
    
    In that case, we would set an uninitialized 4-byte value from the
    stack to net->sctp.auth_enable that can be leaked back when reading
    the sysctl variable, and it can unintentionally turn auth_enable
    on/off based on the stack content since auth_enable is interpreted
    as a boolean.
    
    Fix it up by making sure proc_dointvec() returned sucessfully.
    
    Fixes: b14878ccb7fa ("net: sctp: cache auth_enable per endpoint")
    Reported-by: Florian Westphal <fwestpha@redhat.com>
    Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <dborkman@redhat.com>
    Acked-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
    Acked-by: Vlad Yasevich <vyasevich@gmail.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
